notes: Refreshed in spec 39 (pr-comments hardening v2). The W011 severity rose from medium to high between baseline capture and this rerun against the v1.41 SKILL.md; the underlying mitigations (untrusted_comment_body framing, 64 KB body size guard, diff-context validation gate, screening-independence note, argument validators) are documented in the new ## Security model section. Snyk's W011 fires on the presence of `gh api .../comments` ingestion patterns regardless of mitigations — the substantive default-mode defense is the Step 6 diff-context validation gate (path/line check plus diff-hunk content check) backed by auto-mode escalation to a confirmation prompt on any screening-flagged or oversized comment, or any Step 6 diff-validation downgrade (the path/line `decline`, the diff-hunk-drift `decline`, and the missing-data `fix` downgrade); `--manual` mode additionally restores the Step 7 confirmation gate before any edit, commit, or push. W012 (high) added 2026-05-21: CI's `snyk-agent-scan==0.5.1` consistently reported W011+W012 for pr-comments, while local runs against the identical SKILL.md reported only W011. W007 (high) added 2026-06-22: the same non-determinism that the peer-review baseline documents has now extended to pr-comments — `snyk-agent-scan==0.5.1` pins the client, not the scanner's server-side backend model, so which subset of {W007, W011, W012} it emits varies between otherwise-identical runs (CI emitted W007+W011+W012, while 3 consecutive local runs emitted W007+W011). To keep the deterministic CI gate stable against this flapping, the baseline now pins the SUPERSET of all observed findings — W007, W011, W012 — so any run that emits a subset reads as a cleared finding (an improvement, not a regression) rather than failing CI, while a genuinely new finding ID still trips the gate. This mirrors the superset approach in evals/security/peer-review.baseline.json. None of the three is introduced by a code change here — the only pr-comments SKILL.md diff in this PR is the stale-HEAD ordering fix plus a status-line wording fix, neither of which touches credential handling (W007), comment ingestion (W011), or external-CLI handoff (W012). W007 is the same insecure-credential-handling heuristic already accepted in peer-review's baseline; the W011 mitigations above cover W012 and W007 unchanged.
